source_citation: Heim, I. (1982) - "The Semantics of Definite and Indefinite Noun Phrases"

targets.scope: Independent world/assignment satisfaction and domains; explicit inhabited-domain condition for empty-file truth.
Literal B is preserved; stronger support is proved separately and a countermodel distinguishes them.
Final rules I–IV and proposed V, not just preliminary p.228 universal rule.
Local extended NFC, complex descriptive checks, and partial mathematical updates without a total entailment decider.
File truth, criterion C, existential force and discourse anaphora; classical exhaustiveness only under felicitous true input.
Strong donkey restrictor, existential nuclear closure, negative closure and nonexport; fixed 0/1 representative indices with arbitrary models.
Footnote 21 constructive double-negation conclusion and its classical positive membership conclusion separated.
Entailment quantifies across worlds; description licensing uses the local intermediate file.
Finite interleavings and explicit bridges implemented; selecting contextually acceptable bridges remains a policy input.
Actual definite father syntax, permitted bridge run and derived existential reading; local king-negation separation.
Both local/global calculations and a separating model; no automatic preference invented.
C′ represented with relevance/erasure input; structural weakening alone is shown insufficient for a unique truth prediction.
Memory/proxy interface and dependence on proxy policy; no full integrated recency/acceptability processor.
Literal equality of assignment sets does not follow from informationally redundant new-card accommodation; world-content preservation is proved separately.
Earlier indexed satisfaction and context-reference schema; two family correspondences and text closure, not a whole-system equivalence.
World/assignment human necessity and possibility, contextual accessibility/ordering and classical duality.
The source's best-world/limit assumption matters: explicit unbounded-order countermodel shows vacuity.
Realistic actual consequences, ideality/actuality and factivity separations; not a solved generic or attitude-anaphora theory.

Subject prefixing, indexing/coindexing/scope constraints on supplied syntax and name-scope example. General movement derivations/free-variable extraction are not implemented; crossover alternatives and the source's unresolved specific/generic indefinite exceptions (pp.147–150) are not settled.

requirements.requirement: Predicates for sets, independent domains, typed tuples, recursive updates and an explicit felicity guard.

Best-world existence for nonvacuous simplified human necessity (p.117 fn.8).
For pp.250–251 distinguish unchanged possible-world content from unchanged assignment satisfaction sets; no silent rewrite of the source.
Contextual bridge choice, local/global preference, false-file relevance repair, prominence and proxy licensing.
